name: Chicago
tagline: World-Class Architecture, Deep Dish, and a Stunning Lakefront — At Half the Coastal Price
description: Chicago is the FIRE retiree's secret weapon among major US cities — genuine big-city culture, dining, and architecture at roughly half the cost of New York or San Francisco. The lakefront rivals any coastal city, the food scene punches above its weight with more Michelin stars than LA, and neighborhoods like Logan Square and Wicker Park hum with creative energy. The trade-off is winter: brutal cold from December through March pushes up utility bills and tests your resolve. But those who stay are rewarded with magical summers and a city that fiercely earns its keep.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 200-1000 Mbps fiber available via AT&T and Xfinity
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderately Safe — crime varies dramatically by neighborhood; most residential areas are very safe
quickFacts.nearestAirport: O'Hare International Airport (ORD) — 35 min from downtown; Midway (MDW) — 25 min
quickFacts.climate: Humid continental with frigid winters (-10 to -1°C) and warm, humid summers (22-30°C). Lake effect moderates temperatures near the shore. Spectacular fall foliage.

housing.description: Compact studio or junior 1BR in a transit-served neighborhood near an L stop (Rogers Park, Uptown, Pilsen)

dining.description: Mostly home cooking, with an occasional cheap eat — a taqueria, a slice, a neighborhood diner

healthcare.description: A subsidized Silver plan through Get Covered Illinois, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600; above that, the full price climbs toward $1,000 a month. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A CTA 30-day pass ($85) plus a Divvy bike membership and occasional rideshare — no car

entertainment.description: The gym, free lakefront and festivals, a museum or cinema now and then, streaming

1M.lifestyle: A genuinely frugal life anchored in a compact studio near an L stop, where housing plus a subsidized health premium absorb well over half the budget — the classic American squeeze. Cooking at home is the default, with a cheap meal out as a treat. The car is gone entirely: a CTA pass, a Divvy membership, and the occasional rideshare cover the city, which is exactly what keeps this line lighter than in car-dependent metros. Free lakefront, neighborhood festivals, and the gym fill the calendar.

housing.description: Proper modern 1BR in a settled, walkable neighborhood (Edgewater, Lincoln Square, Logan Square, Lakeview)

dining.description: Out a few times a week at solid neighborhood restaurants

healthcare.description: Subsidized Silver, less aggressively managed, still kept under the cliff

transportation.description: CTA pass plus more frequent rideshare and Divvy; still car-free

entertainment.description: Concerts, a ballgame, nights out, a fuller streaming/gym stack

2M.lifestyle: A settled, unhurried life in a proper 1BR in a leafy, walkable neighborhood. Eating out becomes routine rather than rare, and there is room for concerts, ballgames, and a real streaming-and-gym stack. Transit still does the heavy lifting, so no car payment weighs on the month. Health coverage stays subsidized, with income kept comfortably under the cliff.

housing.description: Quality 1BR in a prime walkable district (Lincoln Park, West Loop, Lakeview, South Loop), often with amenities

dining.description: Dining out several times a week, including chef-driven neighborhood spots

healthcare.description: Priced at the edge of the subsidy cutoff and padded — a richer plan while subsidized, or Silver plus real out-of-pocket; healthcare is the swing variable because a drawdown can push income over $62,600 and vaporize the credits

transportation.description: Transit-primary: CTA pass, regular rideshare, occasional Metra and car-share; a car is still optional

entertainment.description: Theater, sports tickets, hobbies, and a genuine travel budget

3M.lifestyle: A relaxed, financially-independent life in a quality 1BR in one of Chicago's most desirable walkable districts, amenities included. Dining out several nights a week is normal, hobbies and a genuine travel budget are funded, and the city is covered by transit plus liberal rideshare, so a car remains optional. Healthcare is the swing variable: the line is padded because a drawdown can push income past the $62,600 subsidy cutoff and erase the premium tax credits. It is a secure, comfortable rhythm without extravagance.

housing.description: Luxury 1BR high-rise in River North, Streeterville, or the West Loop, with doorman, gym, and views

dining.description: Frequent fine dining across the city's stronger restaurant tier

healthcare.description: MAGI over the cliff — a fully unsubsidized Gold PPO with broad network access

transportation.description: A car enters for convenience: payment, insurance, and a downtown garage spot, alongside rideshare

entertainment.description: Premium events, club and cultural memberships, more frequent travel

domesticHelp.description: A housekeeper roughly every one to two weeks

luxuryExtras.description: Upscale discretionary: premium fitness/club, wine, grooming, shopping, weekend getaways

5M.lifestyle: An upscale life in a doorman high-rise 1BR in River North, Streeterville, or the West Loop, with skyline views and a gym downstairs. Fine dining is frequent, a car finally makes sense for convenience despite Chicago's steep downtown parking, and a housekeeper visits every week or two. Health coverage is now fully unsubsidized — a Gold PPO with a broad network — and discretionary spend covers clubs, wine, shopping, and regular getaways. The city's best is routinely within reach.

housing.description: Prime-district luxury 2BR or penthouse in the Gold Coast, Streeterville, or Lincoln Park — top of the rental market, private-elevator/large-deck tier

dining.description: Near-daily dining at the city's best tables, tasting menus included

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized domestic plan (Gold/Platinum PPO) plus concierge/direct-primary-care — a US-domestic build, not an international expat plan

transportation.description: A premium car with reserved downtown parking, plus frequent rideshare and black-car service

entertainment.description: Season tickets, marquee experiences, and extensive travel

domesticHelp.description: A weekly-plus housekeeper with occasional personal-assistant/errand support

luxuryExtras.description: Luxury discretionary: premium travel, personal shopping, club memberships, a wine budget, a concierge lifestyle

10M.lifestyle: The top of what this budget buys in Chicago: a prime-district penthouse or luxury 2BR in the Gold Coast, Streeterville, or Lincoln Park, private-elevator tier with lake and skyline views. The best restaurants are near-daily, a premium car sits in a reserved downtown space, and full domestic help plus a concierge lifestyle handle the logistics. Healthcare is an unsubsidized top-tier domestic plan layered with concierge/direct-primary-care — no expat plan is needed on US soil. At roughly $224k/year it is unambiguously lavish.
